title: The Winter Feast

recipes.name: Caramelised onion & rosemary palmiers
recipes.total: ~90–120min including onion reduction and chilling; plus day-of refresh
recipes.description: Crisp, savoury bites to serve with clementine-rosemary fizz.

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary
ingredients.note: Approx. 8g picked leaves minced for pastry; ~4g sprigs for drinks. Trial former stronger 20g dose separately.

ingredients.name: Caster sugar
ingredients.note: Only if making the optional homemade rosemary syrup for the drinks.

steps: Cook 350g finely sliced onions in the listed 25ml oil over medium-low heat for a TRIAL 30–45min until deeply golden and nearly dry; weigh cooked yield. Cool COMPLETELY in a shallow dish before filling pastry.
Roll out 300g cold verified-vegan puff pastry; spread THINLY with 20g mustard, fully cold dry onions, ~8g very finely minced tender rosemary leaves (NO stalks) and 12g nutritional yeast.
Roll both long edges tightly to meet; chill at least 30min until firm, then slice evenly ~8–10mm and keep cool before baking.
Bake spaced on parchment around 200°C/Gas 6 for PROVISIONAL 18–25min until deeply golden and crisp THROUGH the central seam. Rack-cool fully; freeze in airtight container.

TESTBED METHOD: at ~11:50 on Christmas Day re-crisp baked frozen palmiers in the gas oven ~170–180°C/Gas 4–5 for an unvalidated 8–12min, until hot and crisp throughout. Rack-cool for 12:30 welcome. Oven must be freed for 12:15 pie preheat. If oven unavailable, use a separately tested fully defrosted room-temperature serving method, never serve frozen pastry.

CLEMENTINE FIZZ (make juice ahead): squeeze 12 clementines, aiming for around 450–550ml juice (the true yield varies). Chill. At service add up to 1 litre well-chilled sparkling water, tasting as you go: it should still taste distinctly of clementine, not watery. Use a little of the reserved ~4g rosemary for garnish. Optional HOMEMADE ROSEMARY SYRUP: simmer 50g caster sugar, 50ml water and 2–3 small rosemary sprigs for 2–3 minutes, cool and strain (roughly 80ml yield); add only enough to balance the fruit. Leave the syrup out entirely if the fruit is sweet enough.
checkpoints: Cool onion filling before pastry
Ensure pastry is vegan
No soggy centres
Test 8g rosemary leaves in pastry versus prior 20g; baked-from-frozen re-crisp at 11:50 must free oven before 12:15
recipes.notes: The earlier 5-fruit to 1L soda ratio was too weak. Juice yield and clementine sweetness vary by fruit; start with about twice as much juice as before and dilute by taste. There is a separate optional 50g sugar allowance only for making syrup when choosing the optional homemade syrup. CHEF TRIAL: Ottolenghi-style slow, dry onion reduction and cold pastry. Record onion cooked weight, rosemary dose, bake and refresh times and seam crispness. Not validated.

recipes.name: Celeriac, parsnip & apple velouté
recipes.description: Smooth, wintery and bright; garnish is added only at service.

ingredients.name: Celeriac
ingredients.note: Peeled weight; expect ~1–1.2kg whole depending on trimming.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.note: Three purchased for comparison: put TWO in the baseline soup; cook third separately ONLY for sweeter variant.

steps: Dice 800g peeled celeriac, 450g parsnips, TWO of the 3 apples and 200g onions. Sweat onion in 35ml olive oil until translucent without browning. Third apple reserved for a separately cooked trial variant, not added raw.
Start with ~1.2L of the listed 1.5L VEGAN stock; reserve 300ml to thin at the end. Simmer roots and two apples ~25–40min until completely soft. Avoid an unnecessarily watery soup.

Blend extremely smooth (strain only if necessary), season and measure final base volume. For 9 small starter bowls aim 9×180–220ml plus modest contingency; freeze excess separately. Adjust with reserved stock only as needed, and freeze WITHOUT 250ml oat cream.

25 DEC — Reheat fully thawed soup, stirring until steaming throughout; add 250ml oat cream and a little fresh lemon to balance the parsnip/apple sweetness, tasting incrementally. Record actual finished ml and lemon used. Crisp sage separately, and offer optional 70g toasted hazelnuts ON THE SIDE for allergens.
checkpoints: Smooth, spoon-coating texture
Freeze without cream
Hazelnuts on the side
Record two-versus-three cooked apple taste, base volume, actual stock/lemon used and nine portion sizes
recipes.notes: Target 9 starter-size bowls (roughly 180–220ml each) before the large roast, not an automatic 300ml portion; the total cooked volume depends on actual vegetable sizes and reduction. CHEF TRIAL: Anna Jones-style balanced celeriac/apple, crisp sage and optional nuts. The two-apple baseline and initial 1.2L stock are provisional.

recipes.name: Fennel, sage & clementine porchetta
recipes.total: Weber indirect roast ~4–5½h plus optional 15–25min crackling and uncovered rest; trial required
recipes.makeAhead: Ask butcher to prep an even belly roll; roll, salt and air-dry uncovered from 23 Dec evening
recipes.description: Skin-on belly, fragrant filling, uncompromisingly crisp crackling.

ingredients.name: Charcoal briquettes
ingredients.note: Have about 8kg AVAILABLE as a winter fuel reserve for long indirect cooking and a possible high-heat finish. Consumption varies; buy bag sizes by total weight, not number of bags.

ingredients.name: Applewood smoking chunks
ingredients.note: 2–3 small clean untreated fruitwood chunks; avoid overpowering smoke.

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.note: For the meat-only drip pan; keep separated from vegan preparation.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.note: For the meat-only drip pan.

ingredients.name: Dry cider
ingredients.note: Drip pan only; the pork jus separately needs its 400ml cider.

steps: 23 DEC EVENING — ASK THE BUTCHER for a neat, even 2.8kg boneless skin-on belly rectangle, rib cartilage removed and unusually thick meat evened out. Ask to take trimmed rib bones home if available, but do not assume they are included. Skin edges should meet without overlap when rolled. Score ONLY the flesh. Spread about 21g of the listed 35g fine salt, all 8g black pepper, 12g lightly toasted crushed fennel seeds, 25g sage, 18g rosemary, 8 crushed garlic cloves and the zest of 3 clementines over the flesh. Optional pinch of chilli flakes or lemon zest is a deliberate, unweighed variation, not required by the shopping list.

23 DEC EVENING — Roll skin outwards into a firm even cylinder and tie with cooking twine about every 2–3cm. Pat skin very dry; rub with the remaining ~14g fine salt. If tested, VERY shallow fine pin-pricks through the rind can help fat blister, but do not deeply puncture flesh. Do not add baking powder by default (only after a test of quantity and taste). Set uncovered on a rack inside a catch tray on the LOWEST fridge shelf, physically isolated from ready-to-eat vegan food. Check adequate fridge space and temperature below 5°C. Keep refrigerated until shortly before cooking; do not leave raw pork out for an hour by default.

25 DEC — Set up Weber Master-Touch outdoors and sheltered from gusts but NEVER in an enclosed space. Default: one charcoal bank/basket to one side with a clear indirect zone under the joint; position a metal drip tray beneath it away from direct flames. Alternatively use a rehearsed 2-wide/2-high snake of briquettes around the edge; a snake is DESIGNED to ignite unlit briquettes progressively, so do not confuse it with throwing a heap of unlit coals into the hot fire. Light the main fire with a chimney and safe firelighters. Add 2–3 optional small applewood chunks for subtle smoke; avoid lighter fluid. Maintain a measured provisional 160–180°C at the GRATE, adjusting vents and adding lit fuel when appropriate, never relying solely on the lid dial.

25 DEC — Aim to place the rolled belly on the indirect side around 08:15, skin uppermost; thickest section nearer the heat. Use one clean food probe in the centre and a separate grate-level thermometer. In the drip tray put the listed 1 onion, 1 apple and optionally 100ml cider with a splash of water to prevent scorching; do not let rendered fat flare on the coals. The tray and drippings are MEAT-ONLY. Take a reading every 45–60 minutes (provisional 09:15, 10:15 and 11:15 checks), adjusting airflow or turning the joint for even cooking. Do not open the kettle more often than required. If the pan begins drying or burning, add a little liquid carefully; skim and boil any collected juices thoroughly before adding to pork jus.

ROLLED-PORK SAFETY FIRST — Cook the centre to at least the UK FSA 70°C held 2 minutes, or an accepted equivalent time/temperature combination, measured with a clean calibrated probe. Beyond that mandatory safety checkpoint, aim PROVISIONALLY for about 85–88°C for a tender, well-rendered belly, checking that a skewer or probe slips through the meat and fat with little resistance. Temperature is a guide to texture, not a guarantee. At 160–180°C a 2.8kg rolled joint might need substantially more than four hours: there is NO promise it reaches tenderness by 12:30. Record actual time and grate conditions during a rehearsal.

CRACKLING — Check core, fat rendering and skin at about 12:20, then decide whether a high-heat finish will be appropriate around 13:00–13:25 (provisional). If the meat is approaching the tender end point, light sufficient fresh charcoal completely in the chimney to make a controlled high INDIRECT heat phase around 230–260°C grate temperature. A full chimney is a reserve option, NOT an automatic instruction: use the grate reading and fuel already alight. Carefully control vents, keep the pork out of direct flame, and observe the skin closely for roughly 15–25 minutes; turn the joint only when needed for even blistering. Move the drip pan safely if steaming liquid would spoil the crackle, but ALWAYS protect against dripping fat flare-ups. If the centre is not safe and tender, continue indirect cooking and push pork later rather than forcing early crackling. The 13:00 start is a conditional appointment, never proof that it is ready.

REST, CARVE AND SERVE — When pork is safe, tender and crackling crisp, remove to a clean rack over a meat-only tray, uncovered and away from steam. Allow roughly 20–40 minutes of rest as a starting range; if ready substantially early, monitor actual food temperature and use a verified safe holding plan, or adjust when the meat is served. Never leave it uncovered for a fixed 65–70 minutes just to reach the carving time, or assume a closed kettle at 110°C hot-holds safely without changing texture. Ideally carve shortly before the planned 14:20 main, around 14:05–14:10, onto a meat-only platter. Serve the VEGAN pithivier and sides on time if pork is still cooking. If any meat is late, the meat course can follow separately.

WEBER TRIAL RECORD (do not substitute rotisserie timings): with a real 2.8kg belly-only roll record diameter, start temperature, outdoor wind, grate/core every 45–60min, fuel added in kg, time above FSA 70°C/2min safety checkpoint, ~85–88°C tender probe response, indirect high-heat finish and final uncovered rest. Keep vegan service independently at 14:20.
checkpoints: Use a properly set up INDIRECT fire with a separate grate probe; wind changes temperatures
Keep pork drip pan, utensils and board entirely separate from vegan dishes
Rolled pork: FSA 70°C for 2 minutes, or accepted equivalent, verified at core
Tenderness goal ~85–88°C is provisional; feel and fat rendering take priority
Crackle only when meat is close enough to done; additional fully lit fuel is conditional, not a clock guarantee
Have approximately 8kg total briquettes available in winter, not necessarily two bags
Conditional high-heat slot around 13:00; uncover and rest for ~20–40min, carve near 14:05 only if safe and ready. No fixed 65-minute counter rest.
Record actual Weber fuel consumption, safe dwell, final skin and tender-probe feel before treating 08:15–13:25 as reliable
recipes.notes: Andrew Clarke's published live-fire guidance supports clean charcoal, zones and small wood additions; this is our adapted Weber plan, not his personal recipe. A one-side fire is the default because it leaves a useful indirect zone; a 2x2 snake is an alternative after rehearsal and relies deliberately on progressively igniting unlit briquettes. Weber's own crackling recipes vary in charcoal amount and often employ different setups/rotisserie: a full chimney is NOT an assured need nor a fixed temperature guarantee. The ~85–88°C core is a texture planning target only, distinct from mandatory safe core/time. The fixed roast schedule is aspirational and temperature/weather-dependent: if late, the vegan main is served independently. When choosing to keep pork whole for extended rest, plan food-safe holding separately. Use suitable heatproof gloves, dedicated meat pan and foil drip tray; do not move a pan of near-boiling liquid in a hurry. Optional saved bones may be roasted and simmered for an improved meat-only stock ahead of time.

recipes.name: Apple, cider & pork jus
recipes.description: A separate meat-only sauce, never placed among vegan sides.
steps: MEAT ONLY: brown 150g shallots in 15ml oil 8–12min. Baseline test uses ONE of the two chopped apples; optionally brown the second for a richer/sweeter comparison. Add 400ml cider, reduce by half and scrape up the flavourful brown bits; record reduction time and apple choice.

Add 600ml pork or chicken stock, simmer 20–30min, strain and reduce again to a balanced pouring jus. Measure yield for 6 meat eaters; shop stock may be light-bodied. Season AFTER reduction, then add the listed 25ml vinegar gradually, starting with ~10ml to counter rich pork without making a sweet-sour sauce.

Cool promptly and freeze in a labelled MEAT-ONLY container. If your butcher provided pork rib bones, roast and simmer them with water and aromatics to make or enrich the 600ml stock in this recipe; otherwise use bought meat stock. On Christmas Day reheat thawed jus in its separate pork-only saucepan until steaming throughout. Skim the fat from any pork drip-pan juices and thoroughly boil them before adding to the jus; reduce and taste. Do not assume captured drippings are fat-free or ready to serve.
checkpoints: Keep meat gravy fully separate
Reheat until steaming
Taste 1 vs 2 apple comparison, record ml of finished jus and vinegar added AFTER reduction
recipes.notes: Optional pork rib bones and carefully skimmed Weber pan juices can give stock depth and reduce waste, but both are strictly meat-only. If bones are not supplied, use the stated stock; do not silently double the required 600ml. Heat any added drip juices thoroughly. CHEF TRIAL: classical browned shallot/cider reduction and acidity-led pork sauce. Second apple is optional taste comparison, not necessary for baseline.

recipes.name: Wild mushroom, chestnut & squash pithivier
recipes.total: ~3–4h across days including two chills; 50–75min oven bake
recipes.makeAhead: Cook filling 23 Dec evening, chill promptly; assemble 24 Dec; bake 25 Dec
recipes.description: A generous 26–28cm pastry centrepiece with a properly dry, savoury filling.

ingredients.name: Mixed fresh mushrooms
ingredients.note: Trial baseline: reduce dry and measure cooked weight. Previous 1100g is a comparison, not volume guaranteed to fit.

ingredients.name: Cooked Puy lentils
ingredients.note: Optional filling variation ONLY if completed filling can fit within dome geometry. Otherwise hold for later.

ingredients.name: Fine sea salt
ingredients.note: Start with approximately 5g in the mushrooms and season the cooked filling to taste; account for salty miso and pastry.

steps: 23 DEC — DRY FILLING: sauté 900g finely chopped fresh mushrooms in TWO uncrowded batches in ~25ml of the total 35ml oil, medium-high, until their liquid is completely gone and they SIZZLE and brown, roughly 15–25min per batch. Weigh the dry cooled mushrooms and record moisture loss.

Roast 250g squash in 1–1.5cm dice with remaining ~10ml oil at ~200°C/Gas 6 until caramelised, 20–30min. Soften 180g shallots and 5 garlic cloves; combine with mushrooms, squash, 250g chopped chestnuts, thyme 18g, miso 25g and up to 15ml sherry vinegar. The 180g cooked Puy lentils are OPTIONAL ONLY after a physical fit check. Start with ~5g of listed 8g salt, taste considering miso. Keep filling DRY, cool promptly in shallow dishes and refrigerate below 5°C; record time for safe holding window.

24 DEC — GEOMETRY GATE: measure volume and weight of ALL cold filling. A 27–28cm pastry base with a CLEAN 3cm sealing margin leaves only ~21–22cm diameter for a low, compact filling mound. Make a small mock dome; record height and maximum pastry stretch. DO NOT force all filling in. Set surplus aside refrigerated for a separate meal, not an overflowing pie; record grams enclosed vs reserved.

Use 850g verified-vegan BLOCK puff pastry, not narrow ready-rolled sheets, roll ~3–4mm thick into a 27–28cm base and a LARGER ~32–34cm lid, adjusted to the actual dome. Form low filling mound leaving 3cm rim; lightly moisten rim with some of the listed 60ml aquafaba, drape lid snugly with NO stretching, press out trapped air and firmly seal/crimp without crushing cut puff layers. Trim rim. CHILL 45–60min to relax pastry; lightly score a fan pattern without cutting through, pierce ~1cm central steam vent and RE-CHILL ~15min before storing cold overnight.

25 DEC — Light glaze: up to 60ml aquafaba + 30ml unsweetened oat milk + 8ml maple; use only a light coat, keep rim clear. Preheat gas oven and HEAVY flat baking sheet ~200°C/Gas 6. Slide cold pie on parchment to hot sheet. Trial bake 50–75min with shared potato tray; lid must be deeply golden, UNDERSIDE browned/cooked and cooked filling steaming hot throughout (a clean probe around 75°C helps assess centre). Rotate cautiously if needed; do not burn top to save wet base.
Rest ~10min, cut three generous vegan servings first, then distribute remaining slices. Log total filling cooked, surplus, pie dimensions, bake time, base condition and actual servings.
checkpoints: Weigh cooked dry mushrooms and final filling (g and ml)
~21–22cm usable dome on 27–28cm base; leave clear 3cm rim
Do NOT overfill: weigh enclosed and refrigerated surplus
850g labelled VEGAN block puff; lid fits WITHOUT stretch
Chill 45–60min; score/vent; re-chill 15min
Preheated heavy sheet; inspect deeply browned base and hot centre
First 3 generous portions reserved for vegan diners
recipes.notes: Use a large block of verified-vegan puff pastry: standard UK ready-rolled rectangles cannot give both the 27–28cm base and the larger domed lid. Do a small pastry rehearsal to check actual gas-oven base browning and filling depth. If the filling is cooked after 17:00 on 23 Dec, cooled promptly below 5°C and baked early on 25 Dec, keep within the FSA 48-hour refrigerated-leftover guidance; record preparation time. Otherwise cook on 24 Dec or freeze in advance. CHEF TECHNIQUE TESTBED: Sally Abé-style snug pastry, cold rest, score and re-chill. These trial filling masses (900g mushrooms, 250g chestnuts, 250g squash, 180g shallots) REPLACE the larger prior baseline to test fitting; weigh actual completed dome and reserve excess. Published smaller pithiviers cannot establish our bake time.

recipes.name: Porcini & shallot reduction
recipes.description: Dark, concentrated and silky, without meat stock or butter.

ingredients.name: Dried porcini
ingredients.note: Soak in about 350ml hot water; strain the liquid through a fine paper filter and use it.

ingredients.name: Vegan block butter
ingredients.note: Whisk in off heat for gloss; optional 5g cornflour slurry if too thin.

steps: Soak 40g dried porcini in approximately 350ml hot water for 20–30min; lift out and pass the liquor through coffee filter or very fine cloth to remove grit. Retain mushrooms and filtered liquor.

Brown 250g shallots and 250g fresh mushrooms deeply in 20ml olive oil, without steaming. Deglaze with OPTIONAL verified-vegan 150ml Madeira and reduce almost away; add chopped porcini, filtered liquor and 850ml vegan stock, and simmer. Strain carefully.

REDUCE the strained stock to provisional 500–650ml concentrated POURING BASE (about 50–70ml for each of nine). Measure real yield and time; aim savoury, not overly salty. Whisk in up to 12g miso gradually only AFTER reducing. Cool promptly and freeze WITHOUT the 20g vegan butter.

25 DEC: thaw then reheat through in its own VEGAN saucepan until steaming; adjust seasoning and thin or reduce as appropriate. OFF THE HEAT mount with 20g COLD vegan block butter for gloss, do not boil hard afterwards. Keep totally apart from meat jus and use its own ladle.
checkpoints: Strain porcini grit
Use vegan-labelled fortified wine or omit
Use separate sauce ladle
Record final finished sauce 500–650ml target, miso used and salinity after reduction
recipes.notes: The butter is a Christmas Day finishing ingredient, not part of the frozen sauce base: thawing can split an early emulsion. If freezing a thicker sauce, concentrate the base by reduction before chilling instead of relying on a cornflour-thickened emulsion. CHEF TRIAL: Anna Jones/Ottolenghi mushroom depth and filtered stock; target yield and reduction time NOT yet measured.

recipes.name: Ultra-crisp Maris Piper roast potatoes
recipes.description: A non-negotiable Christmas favourite; vegetable fat only.
steps: 24 DEC — Cut 2.3kg Maris Pipers into large uniform chunks. Parboil in well salted water until outer surface JUST softens (roughly 8–12min but size-dependent), drain thoroughly, STEAM-DRY for ~5–10min then shake to roughen a thick starchy outside, keeping centres intact.

DEFAULT TRIAL A (Mary Berry-style make-ahead): heat ~70ml of the TOTAL 160ml rapeseed oil in a wide tray; par-roast the roughed potatoes at 200–220°C for an estimated 25–35min until ONLY PALE GOLD. Cool rapidly in shallow single layer and refrigerate. Record how many pieces physically fit in the one tray.

ALTERNATIVE TEST B ONLY: parboil/steam-dry/roughen but CHILL WITHOUT part-roasting, then do one full roast on day. Compare B versus A during rehearsal; do not swap the menu plan without an oven-capacity trial. Kenji's tiny baking-soda addition is an OPTION for a dedicated test only (Maris Pipers may collapse); not a required ingredient.

25 DEC — For default A heat the other ~90ml oil (TOTAL 70+90=160ml, not 160ml twice) at the gas oven's shared ~200–220°C with a truly single-layer uncrowded tray. Add cold pre-roast potatoes CAREFULLY and crisp about 30–55min, rotating once/twice, until all are golden and piping hot. The 26–28cm pithivier must cook on the other shelf: verify both bases and brownings in a realistic trial.

Sprinkle 10g rosemary near end to prevent burning; season across both days from listed 18g salt. Record crunch immediately and after 5min on platter. Do not add a second potato tray if it jeopardises pastry.
checkpoints: Oil allocation TOTAL 160ml: 70ml on 24 Dec + 90ml on 25 Dec
A half-roast/chill default; B parboil/chill alternative ONLY after trial
Steam-dry, roughen, one uncrowded tray for 2.3kg
Test gas oven alongside 70min pithivier at shared temperature
Record 5min after-service crispness
recipes.notes: 2.3kg supplies ~255g raw weight per person alongside a large feast. Increasing to 2.7kg is optional ONLY if the actual tray has room for an uncrowded layer; two trays would collide with the pithivier in a two-shelf oven. CHEF TRIAL: Kenji rough starch crust versus Mary Berry/Oliver make-ahead styles. Compare A and B, actual oven shelf position and tray fit before selecting final technique.

recipes.name: Spiced braised red cabbage
recipes.description: Sweet-sour apple, juniper, vinegar and warming Christmas spice.

ingredients.name: Red cabbage
ingredients.note: Trimmed weight; may need more than one whole cabbage. Weigh raw shredded vegetable for 65g sugar/80ml vinegar ratio.

ingredients.name: Apple cider vinegar
ingredients.note: Start with 80ml and reserve ~30ml extra only if needed at final tasting.

ingredients.name: Light brown sugar
ingredients.note: Start at 65g; balance with vinegar after reheating.

steps: 19–20 DEC — Finely shred ~1.2kg TRIMMED red cabbage (weigh in grams), 2 apples and 300g red onions, 3–5mm even slices. The old 'one whole cabbage' was not a reproducible recipe amount.

Crush 8 juniper berries, add 1 cinnamon stick, 65g light brown sugar and 80ml cider vinegar to vegetables with OPTIONAL 150ml verified-vegan port. Cover and braise gently 90–120min until yielding and glossy, stirring and adding a splash of water only if catching.

Uncover to reduce excess liquid, remove cinnamon and visible spice fragments, taste for distinct SWEET-SOUR balance. Cool promptly, portion and freeze, noting actual cooked weight; do not automatically add the optional extra vinegar before tasting.

25 DEC — Thoroughly reheat fully thawed cabbage close to 14:20 service, provisionally ~13:30 in multicooker. Verify at least 63°C ACTUAL food temperature if holding warm and taste for final acid balance.
checkpoints: Sweet/sour balance
Reheat thoroughly; avoid lukewarm hold
Multicooker model-specific hot hold
Weigh ~1.2kg trimmed cabbage; measure finished batch yield and hot-hold temperature
recipes.notes: Hot holding at ≥63°C must be verified in the actual multicooker. If this cannot be checked, time reheating nearer to plating and serve promptly. CHEF TRIAL: Delia-style slow covered cabbage with apple; measured trimmed cabbage mass replaces unscalable whole head.

recipes.name: Maple-orange glazed carrots

ingredients.name: Apple cider vinegar
ingredients.note: Only to correct a too-sweet glaze, add 2–5ml at a time; may be omitted.

steps: 24 DEC — Trim and cut the 1.2kg carrots to uniform thickness; blanch just shy of tender (trial ~3–6min by thickness). Drain, steam-dry, rapidly chill without leaving in wet water.

25 DEC — Zest and squeeze the 2 oranges and MEASURE the juice. In a wide pan reduce the juice with 10g thyme, starting with only ~40ml of the listed 65ml maple syrup until lightly syrupy. Taste and increase towards 65ml ONLY if needed; don't automatically make a watery sugar glaze.

Add 35ml olive oil and carrots; roll and toss for an estimated 12–20min until thoroughly hot, glossy and tender with little free liquid. Season, add orange zest late and balance with OPTIONAL cider vinegar in 2–5ml increments if cloying (10ml maximum allowance). Reserve a lightly seasoned portion for children; log finished syrup and maple/vinegar quantities.
checkpoints: Bright orange glaze without watery puddles; reduce first
Start ~40ml maple, add up to 65ml ONLY by taste
Acid correction 2–5ml optional listed cider vinegar; log amount
Carrots evenly blanched, thoroughly hot and tender
recipes.notes: CHEF TECHNIQUE TRIAL — Ottolenghi-inspired reduce-then-glaze, not his recipe. Measure orange juice, sweetness, maple 40–65ml, optional vinegar and pan time. Unverified in this kitchen.

recipes.name: Charred sprouts, chestnuts & lemon
recipes.total: 35–45min in actual wide pan; trial 3–4 batches
recipes.description: Crisp edges, fresh acid and sweet chestnuts.
steps: 24 DEC — Trim and halve 1kg sprouts. Blanch BRIEFLY (~1–2min trial), drain and spread on towels in one layer until exceptionally dry. Cool rapidly, refrigerate safely. Compare with raw halved sprouts during rehearsal if blanched sprouts fail to brown.

25 DEC ~13:40 — In a measured large wide frying pan heat small portions of total 45ml olive oil. Add sprouts CUT-SIDE DOWN in only ~250–330g uncrowded batches (3–4 depending on pan); leave undisturbed 4–6min to char, then turn briefly. Move completed batches to a warm DRY tray without a steaming lid. Record how long ALL batches actually take.

Warm 200g cooked chestnuts ~3–5min; return sprouts briefly to heat until all thoroughly hot. OFF heat finish with measured zest and juice from 2 lemons to taste, and 5g ground pepper. Keep lemon bright, not bitter.

PROVISIONAL 13:40–14:15 slot budgets 35min versus previous unrealistic 20min for one pan and 1kg. Peak 13:40–13:55 uses FOUR gas hobs: designate second cook or re-plan if the test proves slow. Never crowd the pan just to meet the clock.
checkpoints: 1kg sprouts must be DRY before pan; test raw-vs-blanched if watery
3–4 uncrowded batches of ~250–330g, log pan size and real minutes
Add chestnuts hot, lemon OFF the heat at service
13:40–14:15 trial; 4-hob peak needs a second cook
Crisp/charred edges without bulk steaming
recipes.notes: CHEF TRIAL: Ottolenghi's batch charring and lemon finish, NOT his separate slow stock-braised dish. 35min provisional; record batch count, heat, raw/blanched comparison and service temperature.

recipes.name: Roasted cauliflower with roasted-garlic miso sauce
recipes.makeAhead: Roast cauliflower and chill sauce separately on 24 Dec; finish 25 Dec
recipes.description: A rich cauliflower-cheese spirit, entirely without dairy.

ingredients.name: Cauliflower
ingredients.note: Aim ~1.2–1.4kg whole / 850–950g edible florets.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened oat milk
ingredients.note: Start with ~350ml, add up to 450ml only to obtain spoon-coating sauce.

steps: 24 DEC — Roast a whole garlic bulb until soft. Soak 140g raw cashews as your blender needs. Trim ONE large cauliflower and WEIGH edible florets (provisionally ~850–950g). Roast uncrowded in 35ml olive oil ~220°C/Gas 7 for 25–35min until deeply coloured and almost tender; Roccbox is optional ONLY after a safe pan-fit trial. Cool promptly; refrigerate sauce separately.

Blend roasted garlic cloves, drained cashews, ~350ml of the listed 450ml unsweetened oat milk, 22g white miso, 50g nutritional yeast, 22g Dijon and 1 lemon. Add reserved oat milk GRADUALLY up to 450ml only for spoon-coating consistency. Record actual sauce ml and taste; store separately. Keep vegan/nut/soy/oat/mustard labels correct.
Toast 90g sourdough breadcrumbs separately with 15g fresh sage to crisp; cool and store completely dry, never in the sauce before serving.

25 DEC ~13:30 — ONE-HOB DEFAULT: warm ALL roasted florets in one genuinely wide vegan sauté pan; add only a spoonful of water and cover BRIEFLY to bring centre hot, then fully uncover and evaporate water. Stir in the cold prepared sauce ONLY for last few minutes, heating everything until steaming hot throughout. Sprinkle DRY crumbs at service so texture survives. This unmeasured one-pan approach gets 30min; test capacity.

ALTERNATIVE REHEARSAL ONLY: if an actually spare verified burner exists, separately reheat sauce and keep cauliflower dry/charred in the pan, spooning HOT sauce over at service. Do NOT introduce a fifth hob on Christmas Day to try it.
checkpoints: Weigh edible cauliflower and finished sauce yield
Brown florets uncovered, refrigerate separate from cashew sauce
Single wide pan finish; uncover to dry before adding sauce at end
Crisp sage-sourdough crumbs ONLY at service
Two-pan sauce variant only if 4-hob test proves spare capacity
Allergens: cashew, soy, oats, mustard, gluten
recipes.notes: Reducing oat milk from 750 to 450ml prevents thin sauce. A large sauté pan may require two batches; the equipment/schedule revision must reserve real hob space. The proposed stovetop finish has not yet been kitchen-tested. CHEF TRIAL: Meera Sodha-inspired soaked-cashew sauce and separated hard-roasted cauliflower; measure one-pan texture loss vs separate hot sauce, without exceeding four hobs.

recipes.name: Crisp sage-and-onion stuffing balls
recipes.station: Gas oven (24 Dec); gas hob (25 Dec)
recipes.description: Crisp individual portions, no animal fats or eggs.

ingredients.name: Vegetable stock
ingredients.note: Use just enough to bind after adding flax gel; do not soak into mush.

ingredients.name: Ground flaxseed
ingredients.note: Mix with 45ml water to form an egg-free binder.

steps: 24 DEC — Sweat 450g finely diced onions (lighter than the former 550g) in some of 75ml olive oil until tender, slightly golden and NO longer watery. Cool fully. Finely chop 16g picked tender sage leaves; 24g is a separate strongly herbal comparison, not the baseline.

Hydrate 15g ground flaxseed in 45ml water for at least ~10min. Coarsely crumb 360g fresh VERIFIED-VEGAN bread without pulsing to paste. Mix with onions, sage, 2g nutmeg, flax and remaining oil. Add ~150–180ml of the listed 220ml VEGAN stock first, then more ONLY if the mixture needs binding; do not make mush. Season with salt/pepper.

Weigh batch and form 20–24 small balls (~40–55g each target), with minimal compression, then bake on parchment at ~200°C/Gas 6 for 20–25min until set and lightly crisp. Test one ball if it crumbles. Cool promptly and refrigerate.

25 DEC — Pan-fry previously cooked balls UNCOVERED in a thin film of vegan oil in a wide pan, turning ~12–20min, until crisp outside and steaming hot inside. Do not use covered steaming or an unreserved oven shelf. Evaluate sage strength alongside cabbage and pithivier.
checkpoints: Coarse fresh vegan bread, not fine paste
450g onions fully dry and cooled; trial 16g vs prior 24g sage
Flax + 45ml water gels; add only as much of 220ml stock as necessary
20–24 small balls; weigh actual yield and centre texture
Pan re-crisp UNCOVERED; hot throughout
recipes.notes: CHEF TRIAL: Nigel Slater's bread texture and sage restraint, adapted vegan with flax. Record herb comparison, stock used, portion count, reheated crispness. Ingredient amounts provisional.

recipes.name: Chocolate-orange vegan baked Alaska
recipes.total: Multi-stage/freezing; up to 60min fresh meringue slot on day is UNVERIFIED
recipes.description: Chocolate sponge, orange curd, vegan ice cream, aquafaba Italian meringue and torch-side theatre.

ingredients.name: Caster sugar
ingredients.note: Allocated: 180g sponge, 100g orange curd, 330g Italian aquafaba meringue.

ingredients.name: Aquafaba
ingredients.note: 220ml FINAL REDUCED, COLD chickpea liquid for two domes; can starting volume varies. Do NOT count 220ml before reduction.

ingredients.name: Cream of tartar
ingredients.note: Provisional ~2.5g scaled closer to Prue Leith's 1/2 tsp for 150ml reduced aquafaba; trial actual foam stability before choosing.

ingredients.name: Caster sugar for optional praline
ingredients.note: For 150g hazelnuts.

ingredients.name: Baking powder
ingredients.note: About 2 level tsp; check brand strength.

ingredients.name: Bicarbonate of soda
ingredients.note: About 1/2 level tsp.

ingredients.name: Apple cider vinegar
ingredients.note: About 1 tbsp to react with bicarbonate.

ingredients.name: Vegan vege-gel for meringue
ingredients.note: ~9g derived from Prue Leith's 6.5g per 150ml reduced aquafaba, PROVISIONAL for 220ml; verify exact vegan product, hot-syrup activation and taste in advance.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened oat cream for optional ganache
ingredients.note: Melt with 150g vegan chocolate.

steps: SPONGE 19–20 DEC — For TWO thin ~18–20cm bases, mix 220g flour, 45g cocoa, 180g of the listed 610g caster sugar, 8g baking powder and 2.5g bicarbonate; whisk 250ml plant milk with 95ml neutral oil and 15ml apple cider vinegar. Combine just until smooth, bake ~180°C/Gas 4 for 22–28min until skewer-clean. Cool fully. Each base should project ~1–1.5cm outside its actual dome.

ORANGE CURD — Heat zest/juice of 4 oranges with 100g of the 610g sugar; whisk 28g cornflour with a little COLD orange juice first, then thicken on heat. Off heat whisk in 65g vegan block butter; cool rapidly until COLD and set. Spread only a very thin layer to avoid wet sponge and melting ice cream.

OPTIONAL GANACHE AND PRALINE — For ganache melt 150g verified-vegan dark chocolate with 100ml oat cream, cool and allow a THIN layer to SET on sponge before curd. For praline, caramelise an additional 80g caster sugar, coat 150g roasted hazelnuts, cool safely and crush; KEEP PRALINE SEPARATE from frozen Alaskas for guests with nut allergies.

MERINGUE SMALL TEST 12–13 DEC, not validated on the full batch — Collect liquid from enough chickpea cans, gently reduce to exactly 220ml FINAL liquid, CHILL completely. Whip with provisional 2.5g cream of tartar to soft peaks. In a separate pan combine 330g caster sugar (remaining of 610g), ~100ml water and approximately 9g of the SPECIFIC brand of vegan vege-gel proven in rehearsal. Follow that product's activation instructions, dissolve completely and heat syrup to 121°C with a calibrated sugar thermometer. With a stand mixer running, drizzle hot syrup in a THIN stream down bowl side clear of whisk, then continue whisking until thick, glossy, ROOM-temperature and pipeable. Serious hot-syrup burn risk. This is adapted from Prue Leith's 150ml reduced aquafaba/225g sugar/6.5g gel formulation; ratio scaling does NOT establish product compatibility.

96-HOUR TEST — Coat a SMALL fully frozen trial ice-cream/sponge dome in the cooled trial meringue, sealing every gap. Freeze in protective rigid container for at least 96 hours, then torch carefully on a heatproof board and inspect weeping, collapse, cracks, off flavour and melting. If the identical formula, brand and freezer storage do not PASS this test, leave final domes UNCOATED until Christmas Day and make fresh meringue near service.

ASSEMBLY 21–22 DEC — Line two 16–18cm bowl/hemisphere moulds holding roughly 900–1000ml each. Pack ~900ml of the listed 1800ml vegan ice cream into each, freeze SOLID, then place on fully cooled sponge with ONLY thin cold curd and optional previously set ganache. Freeze each uncoated dome airtight in a rigid box. Pre-coat only AFTER the actual 96-hour test passed and repeat with exact formula.

25 DEC — If uncoated, begin the TESTED fresh Italian meringue by 14:50 (provisional 60min slot includes whipping, syrup, cooling and coating BOTH domes; log actual time). Have stand mixer, exact gel, calibrated thermometer, piping bag, torch and heat-safe board ready. If pre-coated, confirm frozen coating survived storage. At 16:00 torch briefly from HARD FROZEN on a heatproof board, never on cold glass; keep second dome frozen until needed, slice with warm dry knife and serve immediately. If meringue/ice cream is unstable, omit torch theatre and serve safe un-torched chocolate-orange frozen dessert.
checkpoints: 220ml aquafaba means REDUCED final volume; use enough cans and chill
610g sugar split: 180g sponge + 100g curd + 330g caster sugar Italian syrup; +80g extra praline only
Trial ~2.5g cream tartar, ~9g gel exact brand at VERIFIED 121°C syrup
Stand mixer, thermometer, heatproof torch board and two ~900ml moulds ready
96-hour freeze and torch trial needed before pre-coating; otherwise fresh at 14:50
Trial fresh full TWO-dome coating in <=60min; fall back to un-torched frozen dessert if unstable
Separate optional nut praline, clearly verify all vegan labels
recipes.notes: CHEF TECHNIQUE TESTBED — Prue Leith's vegan Bake Off Italian aquafaba meringue inspires this. Approx. 220ml/330g/9g is an UNPROVEN extrapolation from her 150ml/225g/6.5g formula. Mandatory small trial of gel brand AND 96-hour frozen torch; record actual start-to-coating time for two domes. Default is freeze bare domes and make fresh meringue on day. 2.5g cream of tartar is a PROVISIONAL revised dose.

recipes.name: Pressed potato pavé (optional)
recipes.station: Gas oven (23 Dec) + hob (25 Dec optional)
recipes.description: A restaurant-style flourish, but the first item to drop if timing is tight.
steps: 23 DEC OPTIONAL — Peel 1kg Maris Piper potatoes; use mandoline HAND GUARD to slice evenly ~1–1.5mm. Melt ~110g of the listed 120g VEGAN block butter, reserving about 10g for final browning. Coat thin slices lightly with fat, 8g thyme and salt to taste; layer very evenly in lined loaf tin, recording inside tin dimensions and filled DEPTH.

Cover tightly and bake in gas oven around 180°C until a skewer passes through the DEEPEST centre with no resistance, starting checks around 90min: a deep loaf may take 90–120min OR MORE. Do not stop because a thinner chef's version finished earlier. Cool promptly safely; press under an even weight in refrigerator overnight for at least 12 hours.
Unmould when cold, cut even blocks and test frying in saved vegan fat until all faces crisp without separating layers. Record cut yield and whether blocks hold together.

CHRISTMAS DAY DECISION — Omit from the default 14:20 feast; the main roast potatoes and sides take priority. An optional AFTER-MAIN 14:35–14:55 extra is possible ONLY if every critical vegan dish was served, a burner is genuinely free and a test confirmed crisping works. Never displace sprouts, stuffing, sauces or pithivier.
checkpoints: Mandoline guard; uniform ~1–1.5mm thin slices
Measure actual loaf tin/depth and wait until centre fully cooked
Press evenly in fridge overnight >=12h
Optional AFTER main only; default omit from 14:20
recipes.notes: CHEF TRIAL: Thomas Keller's deeply cooked, chilled, weighted and pan-crisped pavé principles, entirely vegan. Tin geometry and times unvalidated. Default omitted to preserve four burners.

schedule.title: Stabilise Weber one-sided indirect fire. One-side indirect zone set, drip pan protected from fat flare-ups, grate probe stable around a provisional 160–180°C. Do not assume the lid thermometer matches grate temperature.

Roast and probe porchetta. Confirm the rolled pork's FSA safe core/time independently AND assess tender-probe resistance before switching to finishing heat. If not tender, continue indirect cooking; pork may be served late.
Check Weber grate and pork core (1 of 3). Log actual grate heat, pork core, fire steadiness and drip-pan condition; adjust vents or carefully rotate if needed.
Check Weber grate and pork core (2 of 3). Log actual grate/core temperature and burn rate; adjust vents or add ALREADY LIT fuel if necessary. Check for a safe drip pan and unwanted flames.
Check Weber grate and pork core (3 of 3). Log actual grate/core temperature and burn rate; adjust vents or add ALREADY LIT fuel if necessary. Check for a safe drip pan and unwanted flames.
Re-crisp previously baked frozen palmiers and rack-cool. Trial ~170–180°C for 8–12min; oven CLEAR by 12:15 for pithivier preheat. If unavailable, tested fully defrosted room-temperature fallback.
Preheat gas oven and heavy tray. Gas oven and heavy pastry tray have actually reached the trialled ~200°C setting; oven is free of previous dishes.

Assess pork tenderness and prepare lit crackling fuel, only if close to done. Probe tender end-point first; if nearing ready, light enough fully lit coals for indirect 230–260°C as measured. Chimney quantity depends on actual temperature and fire; do not auto-dump a full load.
Serve crisp palmiers and well-balanced clementine fizz
Reheat velouté. Fully thawed velouté stirred until steaming hot throughout, oat cream incorporated; start garnishing for 13:15.
Bake cold, properly filled vegan pithivier on hot heavy sheet

If pork is tender, supervise high-heat indirect crackling. After safe core/time and tenderness have actually been verified, use measured, controlled INDIRECT high heat to crisp the skin; 13:00–13:25 is only the contingency slot. If meat is late, continue roasting and defer the pork; log crackling as skipped/not required only when physically checked.
Finish roast potatoes in the remaining ~90ml oil; inspect shared oven
Serve velouté starter. Starter served with vegan toppings and separate optional hazelnuts.

Rest cooked porchetta, skin uncovered. Rest only after safe, tender pork is off the fire; aim for 20–40 minutes on a clean meat-only rack, without trapping steam. If ready early, monitor food temperatures and use a verified safe holding plan, not a fixed 65-minute unmonitored counter rest. If late, serve meat separately.
Reheat braised red cabbage. Fully thawed cabbage steaming hot through; if held to 14:20, verify hot holding at or above 63°C in the actual multicooker.
Reheat roasted cauliflower; add hot cashew sauce at end, crumbs at table
Refresh vegan stuffing balls. 20–24 vegan flax-bound balls reheated uncovered in oil, crisp and hot at centre; verify holding if kept before 14:20.
Glaze maple-orange carrots. Blanched carrots glossy, hot and tender; if finished early cover in a preheated dish and check still hot before serving.
Char 1kg sprouts in uncrowded batches; add hot chestnuts and lemon
Reheat separate pork jus. Fully thawed pork jus steaming hot in meat-only pan; ladle never used for vegan gravy.
Reheat and finish porcini sauce. Fully thawed porcini sauce reduced if required, whisked glossy and steaming hot in vegan-only saucepan.
Rest and check pithivier before carving. Pithivier has rested ~10min, base checked and vegan servings ready to cut; do NOT carve pork at the same station.

Carve porchetta separately just before service. At about 14:05–14:10 carve on a dedicated meat-only board onto a separate warm platter. If the pork has not reached safe tender readiness, serve it later; vegan main remains on time.
Serve the winter feast. Pithivier and every vegan side plated and hot; serve three vegan adults first. Pork and jus are separate and may follow later if still cooking.
Make proven fresh Alaska meringue for two domes (or check tested coating)
Torch only stable, hard-frozen Alaska domes; otherwise serve frozen dessert un-torched

groups.title: Pork belly oven test (1.2kg slab, gas oven)

items.text: 1 · PREP (about 11:00). Weigh the slab. Score only the flesh, not the skin. Spread on about 9g fine salt, 3–4g black pepper, 5g toasted crushed fennel seeds, 11g chopped sage, 8g rosemary, 3–4 crushed garlic cloves and the zest of 1½ clementines. Roll skin-side out and tie every 2–3cm (if it has rib bones, cook it flat instead). Pat the skin very dry, rub on the remaining ~6g salt, and chill it uncovered on a rack. Note the weight and the rolled diameter: a 1.2kg roll won't predict the 2.8kg cook time
2 · HEAT THE OVEN (about 12:30). Gas mark 3 (about 160–170°C), with an oven thermometer on the middle shelf. Gas ovens run hotter at the top, so read the dial against the thermometer after 15 minutes
items.ifProblem: Move the dial half a mark at a time and note the setting that actually gives 160–180°C.

items.text: 3 · ROAST (about 12:45). Pork on a rack over a roasting tin with ½ onion, ½ apple and a splash of water (50ml cider optional), on the MIDDLE shelf, skin up. Put the probe in the centre of the thickest part. Check every 45 minutes (about 13:30, 14:15, 15:00), topping up the tin so it doesn't burn. Record when the core passes 70°C and holds it for 2 minutes

4 · TENDER CHECK (from about 15:00). Keep roasting until a probe or skewer slides through the meat and fat with little resistance (a texture guide of about 85–88°C core). Don't crackle before this. Record the total time from oven-in

5 · CRACKLE. Move the tin's liquid away so steam doesn't soften the skin, turn the oven to gas mark 8–9 (230–240°C), and put the pork on the TOP shelf. Watch closely for 15–25 minutes until the skin is blistered all over, turning the tin if one side colours faster. Note the minutes and how even it was
items.ifProblem: Next time, dry the skin longer (overnight uncovered in the fridge) or blast hotter; don't shorten the slow roast.

items.text: 6 · TASTE. Was the salt right? Were the fennel, herbs and clementine strong enough, and did the filling stay inside the roll? Note anything to change before scaling back up to 2.8kg
7 · REST AND CARVE. Rest it uncovered on a rack for 20–30 minutes, away from steam, then carve with a serrated knife. Note the rest time, how easily it carved and whether the roll held together
